protocol_name: DNeasy DNA extraction from tissue (nPOD SOP-79, section 1.0)
description: Lyses 8 spleen or pancreas tissue samples with Buffer ATL and proteinase K, then adds Buffer AL and ethanol and loads the lysate onto DNeasy Mini spin columns. The columns are washed with AW1 and AW2 and the DNA is eluted in 100 µL 1x Tris-EDTA. The robot does all pipetting; the operator vortexes, incubates, centrifuges and changes the collection tubes.
assumptions: 8 tissue samples are processed, one per row (A-H) in column 1 of the lysis plate.
A 96 deep-well plate with wells of at least 1.5 ml stands in for the 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes during lysis, so the 8 channels can add reagents to all samples at once.
The 8 DNeasy Mini spin columns, each in a 2 ml collection tube, are held in a 96-position rack (shown as a plate) at positions A1-H1 so the robot can pipette into them.
'All of the mixture' is 180 + 20 + 200 + 200 = 600 µL per sample. It is moved in one 600 µL aspiration with 1000 µL filter tips, so the lysis wells end empty instead of keeping 30 µL.

Filter tips are used throughout, as the SOP lists filter pipette tips. The deck's 300 µL filter tips are used for additions of 200 µL or less, and 1000 µL filter tips for the 600 µL transfer and the 500 µL washes.
A fresh tip column is used for each reagent.
Proteinase K is pipetted from a small reservoir with extra volume for the robot's dead volume.
Whenever an SOP step needs vortexing, an oven or a centrifuge, the operator takes the plate or rack off the deck for that step (sealed if needed) and puts it back afterwards.
Sections 2.0, 3.0 and 4.0 (OCT blocks, FFPE tissue, quantification and storage) are not part of this run.

tips_300.description: 300 µL filter tips for Buffer ATL, proteinase K, Buffer AL, ethanol and TE additions

tips_1000.description: 1000 µL filter tips for the 600 µL lysate transfer and the 500 µL AW1/AW2 washes

lysis_plate.description: Deep-well plate standing in for the 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes; tissue samples in A1-H1

spin_column_rack.description: DNeasy Mini spin columns, each in a 2 ml collection tube (later a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube), at positions A1-H1

reagents.te_buffer: 1x Tris-EDTA buffer, DNase/RNase-free (pH 8.0, 10 mM Tris-HCl, 1 mM EDTA)

steps.instruction: Use 12-15 mg spleen or 25 mg pancreas per sample. Mince further with sterile scissors or scalpel to aid digestion. Place each tissue sample in its 1.5 ml well (A1-H1) of the lysis plate, standing in for a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube, and put the plate on the deck.

steps.description: Pick up tips for Buffer ATL
Add 180 µL Buffer ATL to each sample
Pick up tips for proteinase K
Add 20 µL proteinase K to each sample

steps.instruction: Seal the lysis plate and mix thoroughly by vortexing.

Incubate at 56°C in a hybridization oven with moderate rotation until tissue is completely lysed. Vortex well every 30 minutes. Check level of digestion at 2 hours. If digestion is incomplete, continue 1-2 more hours.
Vortex 15 seconds, unseal the plate and return it to the deck.

steps.description: Pick up tips for Buffer AL
Add 200 µL Buffer AL to each sample

steps.instruction: Seal the plate, vortex thoroughly, unseal and return it to the deck.

steps.description: Add 200 µL 100% ethanol to each sample

steps.instruction: Seal the plate, vortex again, unseal and return it to the deck.
Place a DNeasy Mini spin column in a 2 ml collection tube at each of positions A1-H1 of the spin column rack, open the lids and put the rack on the deck.
steps.description: Set up spin columns in 2 ml collection tubes
Pick up tips for the lysate transfer
Aspirate all of the mixture (600 µL) from each sample
Pipette the mixture into each DNeasy Mini spin column

steps.instruction: Close the spin columns and centrifuge at ≥6000 x g for 1 minute.
Place each DNeasy Mini spin column in a new 2 ml collection tube at positions A1-H1, open the lids and return the rack to the deck.
steps.description: New collection tubes for the AW1 wash
Pick up tips for Buffer AW1
Add 500 µL Buffer AW1 to each column

steps.instruction: Close the spin columns and centrifuge for 1 minute at ≥6000 x g.
Place each DNeasy column in a new 2 ml collection tube at positions A1-H1, open the lids and return the rack to the deck.
steps.description: New collection tubes for the AW2 wash
Pick up tips for Buffer AW2
Add 500 µL Buffer AW2 to each column

steps.instruction: Close the spin columns and centrifuge for 3 minutes at 20,000 x g to dry the DNeasy membrane.
Place each DNeasy Mini spin column in a new 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube at positions A1-H1, open the lids and return the rack to the deck.
steps.description: Transfer columns to 1.5 ml elution tubes
Pick up tips for TE buffer
Add 100 µL 1x Tris-EDTA to the center of each spin column membrane

steps.instruction: Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Close the spin columns and centrifuge for 1 minute at ≥6000 x g to elute DNA. Keep the 1.5 ml tubes containing the eluted DNA.

Network for Pancreatic Organ Donation with Diabetes (nPOD) 
BMSB Room J586 
P.O. BOX 100275 
Gainesville, FL 32610 
JDRF nPOD Standard Operating Procedure 
SOP Number and Version: 79.1          Supersedes: 79.0 DNA EXTRACTION 
Original Effective Date: 05/05/11 
Version Effective Date: 08/15/16 Page 2 of 4 
 
 
DNA EXTRACTION 
 
 
POLICY: Use universal safety precautions when handling human samples and personal 
protective equipment (e.g., face mask with shield, gloves, lab coat or apron).  Use 
chemical and physical safety precautions when working with paraformaldehyde 
and sharps, respectively. 
 
Buffer AL and AW1 contain guanidine hydrochloride, which can form highly reactive 
compounds when combined with bleach.  Clean affected areas or spills with 
laboratory detergent and water, then 1% (v/v) sodium hypochlorite. 
 
PURPOSE: The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to outline procedures 
for extracting high quality genomic DNA from nPOD samples.  
 
SCOPE: This SOP will be applied to the extraction of DNA from fresh or snap frozen tissue, 
OCT-embedded frozen blocks, and formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded blocks. 
 
RESPOSIBILITIES: Managers and supervisors - are responsible for making sure that technicians are 
properly trained and equipment and facility are maintained in good working order. 
 
Laboratory personnel - are responsible for reading and understanding this SOP and 
related documents and to perform these tasks in accordance with the SOPs. They 
are responsible for following clinical laboratory and tissue banking best practices. 
 
EQUIPMENT & 
MATERIALS: 
The materials, equipment and forms in the following list are recommendations only 
and alternative products may be substituted for the site specific task or procedure. 
 
• DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (Qiagen, Cat. No. 69504) 
• Disposable Scalpel, #11 (FisherSci, Cat. No. NC0134996) 
• Microtube 1.5ml (VWR, Cat. No. 10025-726) 
• Microcentrifuge 
• Microcentrifuge tube racks 
• Vortex mixer 
• Hybridization oven or incubator, 56°C 
• 1x Tris-EDTA, DNase/RNase- free (pH 8.0, 10 mM Tris-HCl, 1 mM EDTA) 
(Fisher Cat. No. BP2473) 
• 100 % Ethanol (Molecular Biology Grade) 
• Xylene 
• Absorbent towels 
• Spectrophotometer (BioTek Epoch) 
• Take3 Micro-volume plate (BioTek) 
• Micropipettes and filter pipette tips (10µl, 200µl, 1000µl) 
• Nitrile gloves 
• Safety glasses 
• Disposable laboratory coats 
JDRF nPOD Standard Operating Procedure 
SOP Number and Version: 79.1          Supersedes: 79.0 DNA EXTRACTION 
Original Effective Date: 05/05/11 
Version Effective Date: 08/15/16 Page 3 of 4 
 
PROCEDURE:  
 
1.0 DNA Extraction from Tissue  
1.1 Place tissue in a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube. 
1.1.1 Use 12-15 mg spleen or 25 mg pancreas. 
1.1.2 Mince further with sterile scissors or scalpel to aid digestion. 
1.2 Add 180 µl Buffer ATL. 
1.3 Add 20 µl proteinase K and mix thoroughly by vortexing. 
1.4 Incubate at 56°C in a hybridization oven with moderate rotation until tissue is 
completely lysed. 
1.4.1 Vortex well every 30 minutes. 
1.4.2 Check level of digestion at 2 hours.  If digestion is incomplete, continue 1-2 
more hours. 
1.5 Vortex 15 seconds, then add 200 µl Buffer AL and vortex thoroughly. 
1.6 Add 200 µl 100% ethanol and vortex again. 
1.7 Pipette the mixture into a DNeasy Mini spin column placed in a 2 ml collection tube. 
1.8 Centrifuge at ≥6000 x g for 1 minute.  Discard flow-through and collection tube. 
1.9 Place the DNeasy Mini spin column in a new 2 ml collection tube and add 500 µl Buffer 
AW1 to column. 
1.10 Centrifuge for 1 minute at ≥6000 x g.  Discard flow-through and collection tube. 
1.11 Place the DNeasy column in a new 2 ml collection tube and add 500 µl Buffer AW2. 
1.12 Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 20,000 x g to dry the DNeasy membrane.  Discard flow-
through and collection tube. 
1.13 Place DNeasy Mini spin column in a new 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube and add 100 µl 1x 
Tris-EDTA buffer to the center of the spin column membrane. 
1.14 Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes and then centrifuge for 1 minute at ≥6000 
x g to elute DNA. 
1.15 Proceed to section 4 for quantification and storage. 
 
2.0 DNA Extraction from OCT Blocks 
2.1 Section several thick sections of tissue under DNase-free conditions and place in 
microfuge tube. Proceed to step 1.2 above. 
 
3.0 DNA Extraction from Formalin-fixed Paraffin-embedded Tissue Sections 
3.1 Dissect a small amount of tissue with paraffin from block (0.3 x 0.3 x 0.3 cm3) using 
sterile disposable scalpel.  Cut the tissue into 5-6 equal pieces and place into a 
microcentrifuge tube. 
3.2  Add 1200 µl of xylene and incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes. 
3.3 Centrifuge at 20,000 x g for 5 minutes. 
3.4 Aspirate off the xylene and place tissue pieces on absorbent towels to dry. 
3.5 Weigh the tissue. 
3.5.1 Use 7.5-12 mg of tissue for each preparation. 
3.6 Finely mince the tissue with sterile scissors or scalpel to aid in digestion. 
3.7 Place all minced tissue in microcentrifuge tube and repeat step 6.3.2. 
3.8 Aspirate off the xylene and wash the tissue in 1200 µl of 100% ethanol.  Spin at 20,000 x 
g for 5 minutes and aspirate ethanol.

Original Effective Date: 05/05/11 
Version Effective Date: 08/15/16 Page 4 of 4 
 
3.9 Wash a second time with 1200 µl of 100% ethanol.  Spin at 20,000 x g for 5 minutes and 
aspirate ethanol. 
3.10 Incubate the open microcentrifuge tube at 37⁰C for 15 minutes until the ethanol has 
evaporated. 
3.11 Re-suspend the tissue pellet in 180 µl ATL buffer. 
3.12 Add 20 µl of proteinase K, mix by vortexing, and incubate in the hybridization oven with 
rotation at 56⁰C overnight until completely digested.  Vortex occasionally during 
incubation. 
3.13 Proceed to step 1.5. 
 
 
4.0 Quantification and Quality Analysis 
4.1 Measure optical density at 260 nm wavelength with a spectrophotometer and micro-
volume plate, using 2µl per sample per microspot.  Determine the A260/A280 nm 
wavelength ratio, which should be 1.8 – 2.0 for high quality DNA preparations.  
4.2 Save all raw data.  Import into the DNA Calculator Excel file to show A260/A280 ratio, 
stock DNA concentration (ng/µl), extraction volume (µl), and total DNA yield (ng). 
4.3 Adjust DNA concentration to end-user specifications using 1x Tris-EDTA buffer and 
aliquot stock to avoid multiple thaw/freeze cycles.  
4.3.1 Expected yield from 10-15 mg spleen is 10-30 µg DNA.  
4.4 Freeze DNA and store at -80°C according to SOP Tissue Sample Archiving.

1.2 Biotek Epoch and Take3 Plate Manuals 
1.3 SOP Tissue Sample Archiving
